bullets.title: NVDA -3% on $500B AI Financing Deal; Wall Street Circle-Jerk Narrative
bullets.body: NVIDIA fell to session lows of ~3.2% after FT reported a $500B AI financing partnership with Apollo, Blackstone, BlackRock's GIP, Brookfield, Goldman Sachs, and KKR. At least one fintwit account dismissed the deal as a 'circle jerk' masking weak free cash flow, while others flagged unusual $3M+ call options activity in NVDA earlier in the session. SemiAnalysis separately flagged TileRT inference software on NVIDIA GPUs as a potential competitor to Cerebras and Groq.

bullets.title: AAPL Down 2.5%: Jefferies Downgrades to Underperform; All-Glass iPhone Canceled
bullets.body: Jefferies cut Apple to Underperform from Hold with a $263.66 price target, sending shares down 2.5%. Separately, reports indicate Apple canceled its planned all-glass 20th-anniversary iPhone due to poor production yields; the model had an estimated ASP of ~$2,600 and was targeted for September 2027. Apple is also reportedly testing Chinese CXMT DRAM chips for iPhone 18 Pro, with memory now expected to represent 42% of BoM cost.

bullets.title: INTC -5%: $15B Stock Offering to Fund AI Foundry Amid 14A Customer Traction
bullets.body: Intel shares fell as much as 5.3% after launching a $15B common stock offering to fund AI compute capacity expansion; capex guidance was raised to $20B. Customer commitments for the 14A node process were reported, though one analyst noted 14A cannot proceed on external advanced packaging deals alone. A bold prediction also circulated that major hyperscalers (NVDA, GOOGL, AMZN, MSFT, AMD) will all ultimately use Intel Foundry for CPU production.

bullets.title: MSFT Maia 300 AI Chip Unveiling Set for September; Production Ramp Planned
bullets.body: Microsoft plans to unveil its next-generation Maia 300 AI chip in September as part of a strategy to reduce dependency on external chip suppliers. The company reportedly targets ~1M units but is constrained by TSMC foundry capacity. Unusual activity was also flagged in MSFT stock during the session.

bullets.title: TSM July Revenue +45% YoY to $14.5B; Full-Year Growth Seen Above 40%
bullets.body: TSMC reported July sales of NT$467.58B (~$14.5B), up 45% YoY on explosive AI chip demand. Revenue for the first seven months reached $89.1B, up 37% YoY, with full-year growth now expected to exceed 40%. Separately, TSMC and Sony confirmed a ¥1 trillion (~$6.3B) joint venture in Kumamoto for robotics and next-gen chip production, with Sony holding 60%.

bullets.title: AAPL Testing Chinese CXMT DRAM; TSMC Capacity Sold Out Across All Nodes
bullets.body: Apple is testing Chinese CXMT chips that have cleared speed benchmarks for potential use in iPhones, though it remains uncertain whether Apple will adopt Chinese memory supply. Separately, fintwit noted TSMC capacity is selling out at every node, underscoring AI demand intensity.

bullets.title: GOOGL: $200B CapEx Guidance for 2026; FCF Turned Negative in Q2
bullets.body: Alphabet is guiding to ~$200B in capex for 2026 (roughly 25% of total hyperscaler spend), with FCF turning negative at -$5B in Q2 and management expecting capex to continue rising into 2027. Google Cloud hit $24B in revenue (up from $13.6B YoY) and now represents 20%+ of Alphabet's operating profit. One analyst argues the stock is not 'cheap' at 16x trailing earnings given this trajectory.

bullets.title: Hyperscaler CapEx Forecasts for 2027-28 Have Doubled YoY; $2T Off-Balance-Sheet Obligations
bullets.body: BofA and fintwit analysts highlight that hyperscaler capex estimates for 2027 and 2028 have more than doubled in the past year, providing the clearest signal yet of sustained AI chip demand. A separate analysis flagged that US hyperscalers have signed ~$1T in lease commitments plus another ~$1T in purchase commitments not reflected on balance sheets, potentially understating true capex and debt levels.

bullets.title: META +2.6% on Muse Glimmer Open-Weights Model Release; CEO Champions Open Source
bullets.body: Meta climbed 2.6% to a two-week high after releasing Muse Glimmer, a 30B parameter model optimized to run on a single consumer GPU. One prominent fintwit voice called it 'a very big deal,' arguing it positions the US competitively in open-weights AI and will drive down cost of intelligence. PINS CEO Bill Ready separately argued that any CEO not leveraging open-source models is wasting shareholder capital.

bullets.title: JPMorgan Raises S&P 500 Year-End Target to 8,000; CFRA Goes to 8,650
bullets.body: JPMorgan raised its S&P 500 year-end target to 8,000 from 7,800. CFRA went further, lifting its 12-month target to 8,650 from 7,730 (implying ~12% upside from Aug 7) and its 2026 year-end target to 8,050, citing continued strong earnings. Hedge funds bought global equities for a second consecutive week with gross trading activity at its fastest pace in seven weeks.

bullets.title: Goldman: Memory to Be 62% of NVDA Vera Rubin BoM; Memory Debate Note Circulates
bullets.body: Goldman confirmed memory will represent ~62% of total bill of materials for NVIDIA's next-gen Vera Rubin superchip, with the CPU-side SOCAMM2 module being the largest cost component. Goldman's top tech specialist also published a note on the memory debate. Separately, fintwit questioned what share of $500B in hyperscaler capex will flow to memory and storage names (MU, SNDK, STX, WDC).

bullets.title: SNDK Down 40% from Highs; MU at Keybanc Conference; Memory Cycle Debate Active
bullets.body: SNDK fell from ~$2,000 to $1,200 amid memory market sell-off concerns, with fintwit urging deeper fundamental analysis on HBF roadmap, balance sheet, and buybacks. Micron was scheduled to present at the Keybanc Conference at 10am ET. An analyst also flagged that current long-term memory agreements signal structural differences from past cycles deserving scrutiny.

bullets.title: CLSA Prefers LITE Over COHR in Opticals; COHR 3D Sensing Run-Rate Below $100M
bullets.body: CLSA analyst Briley flagged a preference for LITE over COHR, with COHR's annual 3D sensing revenue run-rate estimated below $100M. LITE separately pulled back from recent highs on profit-taking, insider selling, and valuation concerns ahead of major economic data and tech earnings.

bullets.title: Intel Foundry Prediction: Every Major Accelerator Maker to Use INTC for CPUs
bullets.body: A prominent semiconductor analyst made a bold prediction that all major accelerator and CPU makers—NVIDIA, Google, Amazon, Microsoft, and AMD—will eventually produce CPUs via Intel Foundry, making it the CPU foundry of choice. This comes as 13F filings due Friday will reveal other investors' semiconductor exposure via total return swaps.

bullets.title: Anthropic Forms Internal Chip Team to Use AI for Chip Design
bullets.body: Anthropic is forming an internal chip design team, willing to invest heavily to teach AI to design chips. The initiative is seen as having 3x leverage versus designing chips directly. Anthropic also separately partnered with Macquarie and GIC to build data centers for Claude infrastructure.

bullets.title: OpenAI Launches ChatGPT Business Premium Tier at $125/User/Month
bullets.body: OpenAI unveiled premium seats for ChatGPT Business at $125/user/month ($100 annually), offering 5x usage vs. standard seats, no five-hour usage limit, and weekly usage reset. The company is also offering $100 in credits per premium seat added (max $500 for five seats) as an adoption incentive.

bullets.title: Macro: CPI Wednesday Key Test; July Print Expected at 3.3%; Fed Hike Odds at 46%
bullets.body: Kalshi traders are pricing July CPI at 3.3% ahead of Wednesday's release. September Fed rate hike odds have fallen to 46% from 67% a week ago, driven by weak payrolls, though a hotter-than-expected print could revive the hike narrative. The US 2/10 yield curve hit its steepest level since late May at 45.7 bps.

bullets.title: Strait of Hormuz: Traffic Deteriorates to 6 Crossings; Iran Says No Return to Pre-War Conditions
bullets.body: Confirmed Hormuz crossings fell from 15 Friday to 6 Sunday; Iran's foreign ministry stated the strait will not return to pre-war operating conditions. This drove Brent and WTI crude each up $2+/barrel, with WTI crossing $81 and Brent $86. US SPR fell a record 6.1M barrels last week to 298.7M barrels, the lowest level since 1983.

bullets.title: BOJ September Rate Hike Signal Triggers Coordinated US-Backed Yen Intervention
bullets.body: BOJ Governor Ueda's signal of a potential September rate hike prompted the US to back a rare coordinated yen-buying intervention. The yen subsequently gave back half its gains, falling 0.7% vs. the dollar as Japanese investors continued buying foreign bonds with limited repatriation appetite.

bullets.title: HOOD: Robinhood Chain Surpasses Arbitrum and Polygon on TVL; $300B 2030 Target Thesis Circulates
bullets.body: Robinhood Chain, launched ~one month ago, is already ahead of Arbitrum, Hyperliquid, and Polygon on TVL with ~$488M in daily spot DEX volume and 226K daily active users. Separately, a thesis circulated projecting HOOD to reach a $300B market cap by 2030 (~3.5x upside) by becoming the #1 global trading platform.
